gap: No result ChatGPT got states which of its picks work with Natural Cycles, the FDA-cleared birth-control app. Of its six picks, only Apple Watch SE 3 and Oura do. Garmin Lily 2 Active, Garmin vívoactive 6, Fitbit Charge 6 and Fitbit Air are all missing from Natural Cycles' compatible-device list.
standout_why: I could not open the three cited rival pages. WebFetch was refused for womenshealthmag.com, goodhousekeeping.com and wired.com, and running curl through Bash needed approval. The top uncited results also failed: wearablebeat.com and tech.yahoo.com returned 403. So I could not check whether those pages mention Natural Cycles. ChatGPT's own answer recommends the Lily 2 Active, Charge 6 and Fitbit Air for cycle tracking without saying that none of them can feed a birth-control app. It also never names the temperature-sensor requirement that sets the cutoff. Our current page lists only 'Wrist temperature' for SE 3 and does not mention Natural Cycles. I scored this 2, not 3, because I could not check the rival pages.
decides: For a shopper who wants a tracker that doubles as hormone-free birth control (Natural Cycles, FDA-cleared in 2018), the pick narrows to Apple Watch SE 3 (iPhone only) or Oura Ring 4/5. Oura Gen 3 and later also needs an Oura membership on top of the Natural Cycles subscription. Garmin Lily 2 Active is our pick for small wrists, but it is not on the list. Garmin buyers would need a Venu 3S/4S, Venu X1 or Forerunner 570. Fitbit and Samsung are not listed, and Natural Cycles says not to enter Fitbit temperature data by hand. For shoppers who just want cycle logging, the existing picks stand.

findings.label: Natural Cycles compatibility
findings.value: Compatible. Natural Cycles lists Apple Watch Series 8 and later, all Ultra models, and SE3.
findings.note: Quote: 'Natural Cycles can be used with Apple Watch Series 8 and later, any model of Apple Watch Ultra, and Apple Watch SE3.'

findings.product: Apple Watch SE (1st gen) and SE (2nd generation)
findings.label: Natural Cycles exclusion
findings.note: Quote: 'Apple Watch SE & SE (2nd generation) models do not have temperature sensors.' This matters to anyone buying a discounted older SE.

findings.label: Phone requirement
findings.value: iPhone 11 or later, including iPhone SE (2nd gen or later), with iOS 27 or later. Android is not listed.
findings.source_title: Apple Watch SE 3 – Technical Specifications – Apple
findings.note: The same page says temperature sensing works on Series 8 and later, SE 3 and all Ultra models. The 40 mm case fits 130–200 mm wrists. Apple's footnote: 'The Cycle Tracking app should not be used for birth control.' Perimenopause deviation alerts are for ages 40+.

findings.label: Natural Cycles compatibility
findings.source_title: Natural Cycles Help – Find out if your wearable works with the NC° app (Garmin)
findings.note: Listed Garmin models: Venu 3, 3S, 4, 4S, X1; Forerunner 570, 570S, 970; quatix 8 and 8 Pro; tactix 8; fēnix 8, 8 Pro, 9, 9 Pro; Enduro 3; CIRQA Smart Band. The page states the rule: 'needs to have a temperature sensor and support software updates from Garmin.' Lily 2, Lily 2 Active and vívoactive 6 are absent.

findings.label: Natural Cycles compatibility
findings.source_title: Natural Cycles Help – Which wearable devices are compatible with Natural Cycles
findings.note: Same Garmin list as above. The article says: 'Any other wearables are not intended to be used with Natural Cycles.'

findings.label: Natural Cycles compatibility
findings.value: Not compatible. Natural Cycles says not to enter Fitbit temperature data by hand.
findings.source_title: Natural Cycles Help – Which wearable devices are compatible with Natural Cycles
findings.note: Quote: 'you should not manually log temperature data that was extracted from other wearables (such as Tempdrop or Fitbit).' No Fitbit or Samsung device is on the list.

findings.label: Natural Cycles compatibility
findings.source_title: Natural Cycles Help – Which wearable devices are compatible with Natural Cycles
findings.note: The same list also covers WHOOP MG and 5.0, NC° Band 1 and 2, and NC° Ring.

findings.label: Subscriptions needed for Natural Cycles
findings.value: Active Oura membership (Gen 3 or later) plus a Natural Cycles subscription
findings.note: Oura lists 'Gen2' and 'Gen3 or later with active membership', and says 'You must have a Natural Cycles subscription to use this integration.' The Natural Cycles FAQ (https://www.naturalcycles.com/faqs) says the same: an Oura Membership is needed for Gen 3 and later, and no extra membership is mentioned for Apple Watch or Garmin.

findings.label: Natural Cycles regulatory status and effectiveness
findings.value: FDA-cleared contraceptive app (2018). 93% effective with typical use, 98% with perfect use.
findings.note: Natural Cycles' Garmin and Apple Watch pages say it is a birth-control method in the US and territories, Canada, the UK and other listed countries, and for fertility monitoring only elsewhere. Users must be 18 or older.
